clue.text: Corrupt time-traveller's machine detained in station

indicators.note: something detained in a place is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a base is a station, as in a military or research base
the TARDIS is the time machine of Doctor Who, the BBC's time-travelling hero

explanation.surface: A time machine has been impounded at a station, perhaps for being tampered with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' is a verb here, not an adjective describing the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt something is to debase or adulterate it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Odd characters in britches pose showing muscle

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the words britches pose are taken

explanation.surface: A man in tight breeches strikes a pose to show off his physique.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the muscle at the front of the upper arm.

clue.text: Kind of beach where husband is lost without a partner

indicators.note: the husband is lost, so his letter goes missing from the beach word

parts.note: shingle is a beach of pebbles

explanation.surface: A beach where a woman's husband went missing, leaving her alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being single means unmarried or unattached, having no partner.

clue.text: Something simple to have with tea?

definitions.text: Something simple to have with tea?

parts.words: Something simple to have with tea?
parts.note: the idiom for an easy task is read literally as a slice of sponge served at teatime

explanation.surface: An easy snack to serve at afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a very easy task, and literally is a slice of cake to eat with tea.

clue.text: River reaching middle of Caspian Sea

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: the middle of the word Caspian is its central letter

explanation.surface: A river flowing into the Caspian Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic term for the sea or ocean.

clue.text: Another mistake for fielder?

definitions.meaning: a slip is a mistake, and a second one is another
in cricket, ... is a fielding position beside the wicketkeeper, and the player standing there

explanation.surface: A fielder makes yet another error.
explanation.definitionFit: Second slip is a close-catching cricket position, and also a second error.

clue.text: Block of wood incorporating new pine

indicators.note: a thing incorporating another takes it into its body, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a log is a block of wood

explanation.surface: A wooden block with fresh pine worked into it, like a carpentry description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree, matching the wood, but it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to yearn or ache for it; the verb synonym fits exactly.

clue.text: Oscar holds firm views

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
pinions means restrains or holds fast, especially by the arms

explanation.surface: Oscar has firm views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like part of the definition but belongs to the wordplay with 'holds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions are views or beliefs held by someone.

clue.text: Nerd cut short attempt to secure order in maths subject

indicators.note: the shortened word secures, so holds inside, the order
cut short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a geek is a nerd
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A nerd tries to impose order in a mathematics class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is not sequence but a British honour; 'cut short' and 'to secure' work on the nerd's word before 'attempt' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is the branch of mathematics dealing with shapes and space.

clue.text: Caught on boundary? I had got in, showing excess of this?

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the contracted pronoun phrase has got in, that is entered, the word for a boundary

parts.note: a fence is a boundary
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A batsman caught on the boundary after slogging, the result of being too cocky.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman holed out on the boundary is often guilty of overconfidence, which ties the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An excess of self-assurance is overconfidence, so 'this' stands for the assurance itself.

clue.text: Spies with old word for goodbye

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: Spies signing off with an old-fashioned farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian farewell, used informally in English as a casual way to part.

clue.text: Heads of American classified counter intelligence damage friendly country without meaning to

indicators.note: the heads of the four words are their first letters

parts.note: a dent is damage
an ally is a friendly nation

explanation.surface: Spy agencies damage an ally's interests, supposedly by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by chance or unintentionally is acting without meaning to.

clue.text: Person above the law commercialised prison income irregularly

indicators.note: letters arranged irregularly are out of their normal order, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official is accused of turning a prison into a business and taking money irregularly.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words commercialised, prison and income together are rearranged into the full title.
explanation.definitionFit: This elected official in England and Wales oversees the local force, so stands above the law enforcers.

clue.text: See 12
Essential term in grammar

definitions.meaning: essential means vital or absolutely necessary
the grammatical mood of a verb used for commands

explanation.surface: A key word in grammar lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: It means vitally necessary, and it is also the grammatical mood for giving orders.

clue.text: See 12
Pig-headed, being brought into this world under revolutionary conditions

indicators.note: in a down clue the birth word goes under the other piece
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for conditions is read backwards

parts.note: buts are conditions or reservations, as in ifs and buts
born means brought into this world

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn from birth, raised in revolutionary times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses BUTS to STUB; 'under' puts BORN below it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn people are obstinate and pig-headed.

clue.text: Container whose contents could be scantier

indicators.note: the letters of scantier could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: A container whose contents might be running low.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a metal container for storing food or other goods.

clue.text: Right-wingers which heretics upset

parts.note: that can stand for which as a relative pronoun

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of heretics are rearranged

explanation.surface: Conservatives troubled by a band of dissenters.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Margaret Thatcher, the British Conservative prime minister, were on the political right.

clue.text: Left-winger to outdo as MP

parts.note: a red is a communist or socialist
to cap is to outdo or top

explanation.surface: A socialist hopes to beat a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is not a member of parliament but a military policeman, nicknamed for the red cap British military police wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A redcap is British slang for a military police officer.

clue.text: Shut away fool travelling round Kent area

indicators.note: the fool travels round, so goes around, the area letters

parts.note: a clot is a fool
Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE for short

explanation.surface: A fool is locked up after touring Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To closet someone is to shut them away in private.

clue.text: Insult good chap attending club

parts.note: a brick is old British slang for a reliable, good-hearted person
a bat is a club

explanation.surface: A nice fellow is insulted by someone at the club.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is a piece of criticism, originally a missile thrown at someone.

clue.text: Author occupying position of source

parts.note: to be occupying a place is to be at it
a well is a source of water, so it is the spot where the source lies

explanation.surface: A writer takes up a spot where something originates.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname borne by a writer, so 'Author' points to the person by name.

clue.text: People getting top-class choice of food

parts.note: men can mean people in general
U means upper-class, as opposed to non-U

explanation.surface: People getting a classy selection to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes from which diners choose.

clue.text: Promise showed by goat-herd

indicators.note: letters showed by the word goat-herd are on display within it

explanation.surface: A goatherd demonstrating a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise or vow.

clue.text: People may chat about these motor sport changes

parts.note: F1, Formula One motor racing, with the 1 read as the letter I
replaces means changes or swaps

explanation.surface: Talk about the changes going on in motor racing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of F1 is written as an I. 'about' means around: people gather round these for a fireside chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireside chat is cosy talk held gathered around a hearth.

clue.text: Standard choice of letters from middle of the alphabet

definitions.meaning: a standard is the usual benchmark or expected level

definitions.text: choice of letters from middle of the alphabet
definitions.meaning: the letters N, O, R and M all lie in the middle stretch of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Picking a standard set of middle letters, like a quiz rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the standard or typical level against which things are measured.

clue.text: Buy teapots manufactured in place for tourists?

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A souvenir shop invites visitors to buy teapots made locally.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenic spot that draws sightseers is a tourist attraction.
